name: Trastuzumab
route_note: IV infusion weekly or every 3 weeks; fixed-dose subcutaneous form with hyaluronidase

discovery.by: Genentech (Axel Ullrich, H. Michael Shepard); clinical work by Dennis Slamon (UCLA)
discovery.note: Humanised version of the murine antibody 4D5 against the HER2 receptor amplified in about 20% of breast cancers.

tagline: Targeted antibody that transformed the outlook of HER2-positive breast cancer
summary: Trastuzumab is a humanised monoclonal antibody against HER2, a growth-factor receptor overexpressed in a subset of breast and gastric cancers. Combined with chemotherapy it substantially improves survival in HER2-positive disease and is a model for biomarker-selected targeted therapy.
mechanism: Trastuzumab binds subdomain IV of the extracellular part of HER2 (ERBB2). This inhibits ligand-independent HER2 signalling through the PI3K–AKT and MAPK pathways, blocks shedding of the extracellular domain and promotes receptor internalisation.

Its IgG1 Fc portion recruits immune effector cells, producing antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity against HER2-overexpressing tumour cells. Benefit is confined to tumours with HER2 protein overexpression or gene amplification.
uses: HER2-positive early breast cancer (adjuvant and neoadjuvant)
HER2-positive metastatic gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma

history.title: HER2 amplification linked to prognosis
history.detail: Slamon and colleagues report that HER2/neu amplification predicts poor outcome in breast cancer.

history.title: Humanisation
history.detail: Genentech humanises the 4D5 antibody, producing trastuzumab.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved as Herceptin for HER2-overexpressing metastatic breast cancer.

history.title: Adjuvant trials
history.detail: HERA, NSABP B-31 and NCCTG N9831 show large reductions in recurrence in early breast cancer.

history.title: Adjuvant approval
history.detail: FDA approves trastuzumab for adjuvant treatment of HER2-positive early breast cancer.

history.title: Gastric cancer
history.detail: Approved for HER2-positive metastatic gastric cancer after the ToGA trial.

history.title: Subcutaneous form
history.detail: Subcutaneous Herceptin approved in the EU; Herceptin Hylecta follows in the US in 2019.

history.title: Biosimilars
history.detail: First biosimilars approved: Ontruzant in the EU and Ogivri in the US.

pk.metabolism: Proteolytic catabolism to peptides and amino acids (no CYP metabolism)
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody; cleared by catabolism and target-mediated uptake

safety.boxed_warning: Cardiomyopathy, infusion reactions, embryo-fetal toxicity and pulmonary toxicity.

facts: Benefit is limited to tumours with HER2 overexpression or amplification, so HER2 testing is required before use.
Cardiotoxicity is increased when trastuzumab is combined with anthracyclines, so cardiac function is monitored.
The story of its development was dramatised in the 2008 film 'Living Proof'.
